title: Flat degree-zero scalar comparison agrees between module-object and ringed-site conventions
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,J)$ be a site small in the chosen module universe [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention], let $\varphi:R\to B$ be a morphism of sheaves of commutative rings, and use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] with sheafified sectionwise tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Put $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ with tensor $\otimes_R$ and unit $R$. Regard $R$ as the unit monoid and $B$ as a commutative monoid of $\mathcal A$ via $\varphi$. Identify modules over the unit monoid with $\mathcal A$ by the unit action, and $B$-module objects of $\mathcal A$ with sheaves of $B$-modules by their given actions. Let $E_{\mathrm{mon}}$ be the coequalizer extension of [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars] under these identifications, and let $E_{\mathrm{sec}}(M)=B\otimes_R M$ have $B$ acting on the first factor. There is a natural $B$-linear isomorphism
$$e_M:E_{\mathrm{mon}}(M)\xrightarrow{\sim}E_{\mathrm{sec}}(M)$$
whose composite with the balancing-coequalizer projection is the identity on the local pure tensors $b\otimes m$.

Let $M$ be any flat $R$-module sheaf [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Then $M[0]$ is K-flat for the two-sided quasi-isomorphism convention [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso] as well as for the acyclic-total-tensor convention [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories with localization functors $Q_R,Q_B$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For total left derived extensions $L E_{\mathrm{mon}}$ and $L E_{\mathrm{sec}}$ with their canonical comparison counits, interpreted respectively by [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] and the ringed-site change of rings [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], let $e^{\mathbf L}:L E_{\mathrm{mon}}\xrightarrow{\sim}L E_{\mathrm{sec}}$ denote the comparison induced by $e$ and preserving these counits. The degree-zero comparisons $c_{\mathrm{mon},M}$ and $c_{\mathrm{sec},M}$, each directed from the derived extension of $Q_R(M[0])$ to $Q_B((E(M))[0])$, are isomorphisms and satisfy
$$c_{\mathrm{sec},M}\circ e^{\mathbf L}_{Q_R(M[0])}=Q_B(e_M[0])\circ c_{\mathrm{mon},M}.$$
This equality is natural for morphisms between flat module sheaves. No local freeness of $M$ and no flatness of $B$ over $R$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 03ER (definition-flat), item (3); agent-extracted convention-comparison argument from the returned parent proof Step 4, using section-tensor-product and sites-cohomology.tex lemma-derived-base-change. The module-object convention is blueprint sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars, clause (2), and its derived convention is sk-def-sfb-derived-categories.

proof.text: Write $T_M=B\otimes_R M$ for the sheafified tensor. In the coequalizer of [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars] the middle monoid is the tensor unit $R$ of $\mathcal A$, not an additional coefficient ring. The two arrows $B\otimes_R R\otimes_R M\rightrightarrows T_M$ send a local generator $b\otimes r\otimes m$ respectively to $b\varphi(r)\otimes m$ and $b\otimes rm$. These are equal by the balancing relation in the sectionwise tensor over $R(U)$; sheafification therefore makes the arrows equal, by [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. If $q_M:T_M\to E_{\mathrm{mon}}M$ is their coequalizer, the identity of $T_M$ equalizes them and gives a unique $e_M$ with $e_Mq_M=1$. Conversely $q_Me_Mq_M=q_M$, and uniqueness in the coequalizer property gives $q_Me_M=1$. Thus $e_M$ is an isomorphism and $e_Mq_M(b\otimes m)=b\otimes m$.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product; blueprint def-sfb-modobj-extension, coequalizer formula

proof.text: The action on the coequalizer in [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars] is induced by multiplication on the first factor. Hence, after precomposition with $B\otimes_R q_M$, both sides of the $B$-linearity equation for $e_M$ send $b'\otimes b\otimes m$ to $b'b\otimes m$. Equivalently $q_M$ and its inverse respect this action, by the same coequalizer uniqueness. For a module map $f:M\to N$, both $e_NE_{\mathrm{mon}}(f)q_M$ and $(1_B\otimes f)e_Mq_M$ send $b\otimes m$ to $b\otimes f(m)$, so they agree and coequalizer uniqueness gives naturality. These computations define maps of the sectionwise tensor presheaves and then of their sheafifications [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]; they do not assert that arbitrary sheaf sections are global pure tensors. We have a natural $B$-linear isomorphism $e:E_{\mathrm{mon}}\xrightarrow{\sim}E_{\mathrm{sec}}$.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product; blueprint def-sfb-modobj-extension, induced maps and first-factor action

proof.text: For flat $M$, the additive functor $F_M=(-)\otimes_R M$ is exact by [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology], $H^n(F_MK)\cong F_M(H^nK)$ naturally in $K$. It follows that $F_M$ applied termwise preserves quasi-isomorphisms, and sends acyclic complexes to acyclic complexes. In the total tensor of [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso], $K\otimes_R M[0]$ has just the summand $K^n\otimes_R M$ in degree $n$, with differential $d_K\otimes1$. The other order has just $M\otimes_R K^n$ and differential $1\otimes d_K$, since $(-1)^0=1$; the sectionwise flip $m\otimes k\mapsto k\otimes m$ gives a chain isomorphism with $F_MK$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Thus tensoring with $M[0]$ on either side preserves every quasi-isomorphism. Tensoring any acyclic $K$ with $M[0]$ is acyclic as well. These are exactly the two required K-flat predicates [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso, def-pc-kflat-complex].

source.place: Tag 010N, lemma-exact-functor; sites-modules.tex Tag 03ER, definition-flat (3); sites-cohomology.tex Tag 06YQ, lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat, degree-zero case

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] to $\varphi:R\to B$ on the given site. Its extension is written $(-)\otimes_R B$; the sectionwise flip $m\otimes b\mapsto b\otimes m$ identifies this with $E_{\mathrm{sec}}$, respecting the $B$ action and the differentials [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Since $M[0]$ is K-flat in the acyclic-total-tensor sense, its identity is a K-flat resolution [def-pc-kflat-complex]. The canonical resolution comparison in [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] therefore says that the comparison counit at $M[0]$ is an isomorphism. Termwise scalar extension of $M[0]$ is $(E_{\mathrm{sec}}M)[0]$, so this counit is precisely $c_{\mathrm{sec},M}:LE_{\mathrm{sec}}Q_R(M[0])\to Q_B((E_{\mathrm{sec}}M)[0])$. The cited theorem assumes no flatness of $B$.

source.place: Tag 06YY, lemma-derived-base-change, identity-topos change of rings; derived.tex Tag 06XN, lemma-find-existence-computes, identity K-flat resolution

proof.text: Let $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{mon}}$ and $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{sec}}$ be the given total-left-derived counits, and let $\eta_K=Q_B(e_K)$, where $e_K$ applies $e$ termwise. Use the universal counit property spelled out in [def-sfb-left-derived-functor]: composition with $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{sec}}$ bijects transformations $V\to LE_{\mathrm{sec}}$ with transformations $VQ_R\to Q_BE_{\mathrm{sec}}$. Taking $V=LE_{\mathrm{mon}}$ and $\eta\varepsilon_{\mathrm{mon}}$ gives a unique transformation $a$ satisfying $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{sec}}(aQ_R)=\eta\varepsilon_{\mathrm{mon}}$. Using $\eta^{-1}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{sec}}$ and the other universal property gives $b$ in the reverse direction. Then $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{mon}}(baQ_R)=\varepsilon_{\mathrm{mon}}$ and $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{sec}}(abQ_R)=\varepsilon_{\mathrm{sec}}$; injectivity of the same bijections gives $ba=1$ and $ab=1$. Therefore $a=e^{\mathbf L}$ is the unique counit-preserving natural isomorphism. This uses the total derived functors in the statement, not an exactness claim about scalar extension.

source.place: Total left derived functor and its universal comparison counit; explicit universal-property argument written by Q42

proof.text: Evaluate the counit equation from Step 5 at $M[0]$. Termwise $e$ there is $e_M[0]$, so it gives exactly $c_{\mathrm{sec},M}\circ e^{\mathbf L}_{Q_R(M[0])}=Q_B(e_M[0])\circ c_{\mathrm{mon},M}$. The left-hand factors and $Q_B(e_M[0])$ are isomorphisms by Steps 1, 4 and 5 and functoriality of $Q_B$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Consequently $c_{\mathrm{mon},M}=Q_B(e_M[0])^{-1}c_{\mathrm{sec},M}e^{\mathbf L}_{Q_R(M[0])}$ is an isomorphism. For a map $f:M\to N$ between flat sheaves, the maps $f[0]$ are chain maps; naturality of the two counits [def-sfb-left-derived-functor] and of $e,e^{\mathbf L}$ gives the naturality squares for both degree-zero comparisons and the displayed equality. Flatness was used only for $M[0]$ (and $N[0]$ for this naturality assertion), with neither finite rank nor local freeness required.

The item is unsplit in both live and side-live, is not on the drop list, has no repair note of its own, and the dependency closure has no cycle. Statement, stmt_deps, source and blueprint are unchanged, and proof_deps equals the union of the step uses. I checked all six steps against the cited statements. Step 1: in Mod(R) the two coequalizer arrows B⊗R⊗M⇉B⊗_RM are equal by balancing at presheaf level, so the coequalizer is split by the identity and e_M q_M=1 on pure tensors. Step 2: B-linearity and naturality follow from coequalizer uniqueness (B⊗q_M is an epimorphism because B⊗- is a left adjoint). Step 3: flat means exact tensoring (def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules), and the Mathlib leaf from Tag 010N (lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology) gives preservation of quasi-isomorphisms and of acyclicity. I verified the total-tensor signs for M[0] on both sides ((-1)^0, d_M=0), so both K-flat predicates (def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso and def-pc-kflat-complex) hold. Step 4: clause (2) of lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings with the identity K-flat resolution makes the counit at M[0] an isomorphism, the flip to the B⊗- convention is B-linear, and B is arbitrary. Step 5: the derived comparison e^L is built from the universal property of def-sfb-left-derived-functor; I checked the arrows a and b and that ba=1 and ab=1 follow from uniqueness. Step 6: the displayed equation is the counit equation at M[0], c_mon is an isomorphism as a composite of isomorphisms, and naturality follows. Edge cases: M=0, B=0, φ=id, Z→Z/2 with M=Z or Z[1/2] all agree, and M=Z/2 is correctly excluded by flatness. Stacks tags 03EK, 03ER, 06YQ, 06YY, 06XN and 010N are confirmed, no SGA is cited, and the coefficient categories Mod(R) and Mod(B) are matched exactly.
